title: How do we write the packets of rice as one expression?
description: A packer already has four packets and fills more from one hundred kilograms of rice in two kilogram packets, and the total is written as one expression, split into terms and worked out. Keeko's doubt is that the old packets are added first, before the division.
teaching_notes: One idea: a division stays inside its term, so the division is worked out before the plus. Ask the child why four plus one hundred cannot be joined before dividing by two.

source: {{NAME_1}} packs 100 kg of rice into 2 kg packets and already has
video_script.why: The child sees an expression with a single term and a division term written, split into terms and valued by working out the division first.
video_script.substitution: Change the weight of rice and the size of the packet and the method stays the same; the division is a term and is worked out before the plus.
video_script.anchor: one hundred kilograms of rice, two kilogram packets, and four packets already filled
video_script.wrong_answer: we add the old packets first, so four plus one hundred comes first
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko joins the four old packets with the one hundred kilograms first, so the old packets get divided by two as well.
video_script.payoff_line: There are fifty four packets now.

final_answer.spoken: four plus one hundred divided by two is fifty four packets, with terms four and one hundred divided by two

names.{{NAME_1}}: everyday child, not a character of the book

video_script.design: One idea: a division is part of its term, so it is worked out before the plus. The sack and the packets stay in the anchor band; the working band writes the expression, its terms and its value. Keeko's doubt: add the old packets first.

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>{{NAME_1}} packs one hundred kilograms of rice.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each packet holds two kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Four packets are already filled.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>How can we write the number of packets as one expression?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the sack of 100 kg split into packets of 2 kg; the 4 old packets set apart from the new packets

marks.m1: the sack is split into packets of 2 kg
marks.m2: the 4 old packets are set apart on the left
marks.m3: the new packets are marked as 100 divided by 2

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The rice is shared into packets of two kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The four old packets are already there.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The new packets come from dividing one hundred by two.

beats.on_screen: Given: 100 kg of rice; 2 kg in each packet; 4 packets already filled

marks.m1: the rice and the packet size are written
marks.m2: the 4 filled packets are written under them

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, there are one hundred kilograms of rice, and each packet holds two kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four packets are already filled.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of packets as an expression; its terms; its value

marks.m1: the three things to find are written under the given lines

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to write the number of packets as an expression, list its terms and find its value.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: new packets = 100 ÷ 2; old packets = 4; packets now = 4 + 100 ÷ 2

marks.m2: old packets = 4 is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the new packets are one hundred divided by two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The old packets are four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The packets now are four plus one hundred divided by two.

marks.m1: the plus sign in 4 + 100 ÷ 2 is circled
marks.m2: 4 and 100 ÷ 2 are each boxed as a term

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the terms are the parts separated by the plus sign.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The terms are four, and one hundred divided by two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: work out the division term first: 100 ÷ 2 = 50, so the value is 4 + 50

marks.m2: 4 + 50 is written, ready to be added

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, work out the division term first.
One hundred divided by two is fifty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The value is then four plus fifty.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: add the two terms 4 and 50

marks.m1: the two terms 4 and 50 are joined by a plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, add the two terms together, four and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Four plus fifty is fifty four.
There are fifty four packets now.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The expression is four plus one hundred divided by two.
Its terms are four, and one hundred divided by two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the shelf of packets
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 4 + 100 first, then ÷ 2; 104 ÷ 2 = 52 shown with the 4 old packets also cut in half; the bubble is struck through

marks.m2: 104 ÷ 2 is shown and the 4 old packets are halved
marks.m3: the bubble is struck through and the 4 old packets stay whole

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks we add the old packets first, so four plus one hundred comes first.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But then one hundred and four is divided by two, and that divides the old packets as well.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The old packets are already filled, so only the rice is divided.
